title: Bijectivity of specified unit-cohomology transport through a scheme isomorphism
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, d:X→Y a scheme isomorphism [def-pc-scheme], f:Y→Spec R and fprime:X→Spec R with d followed by f equal to fprime, M a module on Y, and e:M≅O_Y. For every n≥0, unitCohomologyPullbackLinear(f,fprime,d,hd,M,e.hom followed by unitToPushforwardObjUnit d,n) [def-pbc-unit-cohomology-pullback-linear] is bijective. The statement concerns only invertibility of this specified map, and has no cartesian-square or comparison-compatibility conclusion.

source.place: cohomology-equation-functorial; exact inverse-image action on Ext, and Mathlib adjunction and unit pullback APIs

proof.text: The equivalence of opens induced by the scheme isomorphism is cocontinuous in both directions, since its inverse preserves covering sieves. It is a dense subsite, so continuous abelian-sheaf pushforward is an equivalence. Its left adjoint invImage is therefore an equivalence, and Sheaf.H.mapFunctor_bijective applies.

The structural unit module map has components with underlying functions d.app U, all bijective because d is a scheme isomorphism. The componentwise criterion makes it a module isomorphism. Compose it with e.hom and forget to abelian sheaves. The adjoint coefficient is invImage.map of this isomorphism followed by the invertible counit, hence is an isomorphism. Apply the cohomology functor and compose its bijection with the Ext-action bijection. The underlying function of the defined linear map is exactly this composite.

proof_origin.place: Original equivalence and coefficient-isomorphism argument, formalized using Mathlib dense subsite, adjunction and cohomology functor APIs; independent second reading by C3.
